If they are acquitted, all their rights are going to be reinstated; but if they are sentenced to a prison of about two years without the possibility of a parole, or for more than two years, then the service will be terminated under the law. If they are sentenced to a term of imprisonment less than two years, they will serve this sentence in a special institution where the convicted servicemen serve their sentences.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What I'm interested in, and you touched upon one of the elements. I'm talking about the procedural differences. So if somebody is accused of a crime, they would be entitled to have a trial, correct, to see whether the charges were founded or not founded?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would they be entitled to counsel under those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, when a person is retired because they have served 30 years in the service and the needs of the service require their termination, would they be entitled to a trial?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said in the previous discussion that they have the right to institute administrative proceedings before the competent court. At the time that was the supreme military court. They could file for a lawsuit, that is to say, file a charge to the supreme military court, and to request it to deliberate and decide on the legality of the termination of service.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I want to stay with this document, Prosecution Exhibit 2203, and I would like to turn to another portion of this. If we could turn to English page 7, and B/C/S page 46 and 47.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I want to direct your attention to a certain paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The Court -- I'm interested in directing Your Honours attention to the paragraph in the middle which is General Perisic, and it says: "We can conclude the following four were done..." and it goes on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, I believe that starts at the last paragraph at the bottom of the page, and if you would let me know when we need to turn the page, we can do so.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we can turn in the Serbian version to the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In this text, General Perisic says in the third line down in the English, he says: "For those that are going for disciplinary liability, for them disciplinary and criminal, to finish with the investigation. That means for all those who have any elements criminal and disciplinary liability, to finish that." So can you comment on that particular passage in respect of General Perisic's authority to make such a -- take such a position?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm again objecting to this line of questioning, asking the witness to comment on the text. I would kindly ask Mr. Harmon to put a very specific question to this witness. A while ago, Your Honours, when you criticized me of being too long in my objection, if Mr. Harmon, for example, wants to ask the witness whether Mr. Perisic can issue a disciplinary measure against the member of some other army, why doesn't he ask him straightforwardly without reading first the document which actually doesn't serve as a source for this document. Now, I am afraid that once again if you want a comment from the witness, you are asking him to guess, unless Mr. Harmon can put a very specific question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me be clear, Mr. Lukic, that I really do understand what you want. I thought earlier than the time when you say I criticized you, your objection was you don't want Mr. Harmon to quote from the document because the document is still MFI'd, and because if he does do that, then he is putting on the record that which is still to be decided upon. Now, I thought this question that he is asking is specific without quoting the document. Now, but it looks as if you are combining two bases for objection because now you are saying he must not ask the witness to comment. Earlier you are saying he must not quote the document. Could you just refine your objection. Let's understand where the problem is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't want this to be connected with my previous objection. I completely understood that, and I completely understood your decision how these portions of the transcript are going to be treated. However, when Mr. Harmon asked do you have any comment on this specific part of the transcript read out to the witness is simply the question that cannot be understood. Now the witness is asked to pick up certain words and interpret them. I'm simply asking Mr. Harmon to put a specific question, and I made my comment with relation to my previous objection. It wouldn't have happened at all had Mr. Harmon asked this question about Mr. Perisic's capability of punishing any member of any other army without resorting to any document because it has nothing to do with any document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, are you able to respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'll try to reframe the question. Perhaps I will have greater success.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, the passage that you've read, General Perisic refers to continuing and finishing with disciplinary and criminal investigations. Is there anything in that reference that you've read that is inconsistent with General Perisic's authorities as the chief of the VJ General Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is not consistent in terms of the tone that he is using when he is speaking about criminal investigations. I already mentioned that within the scope of criminal responsibility, he can only initiate criminal responsibility by filing a criminal report to the Prosecutor's Office in charge. However, bearing in mind the manner that was applied at the time, and that was the time when I was in the army as well, I understand this language precisely in this way as a sort of launching initiative to proceed in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, in this text as well, there is a reference to misdeeds, and it refers to people who have committed misdeeds, soldiers particularly. And the text that is before me in English says: "... if yes, then negative grades should be given, and the procedure to be expelled from the army should be started, and for those under investigation when time would come for criminal responsibility, they should be prosecuted, as disciplinary..." and it goes on. Let me just get your views. If misdeeds of a soldier are of a criminal or disciplinary nature, what is the system in the VJ to expel somebody from the army under those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about the assessment procedure, each professional soldier who receives two successive negative grades must leave the army. Therefore, professional soldiers are being assessed at certain specific intervals. If one gets two successive negative grades, end up in the termination of the service. I already explained how the services terminated in the case of criminal responsibility and that it is dependent on the conclusion of the criminal proceedings. Speaking of disciplinary proceedings, there are two punishments that can end with the termination. One of the punishments is to take away the rank from this officer, which automatically entails the termination of service. And the other punishment is the loss of the status of a professional soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Based on your experience in the army, was there a preference as to the manner of proceeding? In other words, you've described to us evaluations and negative evaluations, and in some cases if you have two, you can be expelled from the army. There are also, as we know, disciplinary and criminal proceedings. My question to you, Mr. Starcevic: Was there, in your experience, a preferred manner of proceeding?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least while I was in the army there were no preferences in terms of the applicable procedures. It was simply dealt with on a case-by-case basis. I have to say though, that there was certainly legal protection provided for all persons who faced the loss of employment. So all these cases took place to a certain extent and in line with the specific circumstances. I cannot say that either of these were favoured because these procedures were actually meant in order to provide the protection for the service, and they were applied only when it was really necessary and required, when there were really such circumstances that warranted their application. I'm talking about the period while I was in the service, and I presume that all the honourable officers applied these procedures in the same way afterwards, because this is, in a way, rather unexpected termination of employment which suddenly deprives a person of the means for supporting himself and his family and all the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me turn to a different, a final passage in this collegium.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could go to page 7 of the English and pages 46 and 47 of the B/C/S. I'm sorry, I've given you the wrong reference. In English, page 10, and page 49 of the B/C/S, so excuse me for that. And I'm directing Your Honours' attention to the passage at the top, General Perisic, it starts with: "What else, and only lawyers..."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Starcevic, do you see that portion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would like to just direct you to the first paragraph, the paragraph that ends with the words "... the entire situation." So it's the one paragraph I'm directing Your Honours' attention to, and Mr. Starcevic, your attention to as well.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me, first of all, Mr. Starcevic, direct your attention to the passage that relates to: "People who remain in the army for whom there is certain criminal responsibility," you see that portion? It should be about the middle of the text, and it goes on to say, "... grade them with an extraordinary grade, a negative one --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- "naturally, to create conditions to expel them from the army." Again, Mr. Starcevic, when there is certain criminal responsibility of somebody serving in the army not possible but certain criminal responsibility, in your experience, what is the manner in which to proceed under those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, I have no experience under such circumstances, because there a certain degree of criminal responsibility. It is the duty of the Prosecutor to check that. If there isn't, then it cannot be substituted by a negative grade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, in this case, in this text, we also see that General Perisic indicates that he is going to send out an order which he will later sign, and he has given an oral order in the course of his remarks in this paragraph; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We break at 5.15, Your Honour, before I come to my next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed we do. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, if --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: First of all, could we go into private session at this point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 9473 on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Starcevic, this is a document I know you have not seen before, so if you would just take your time and read through this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If could you scroll down on the English version a bit, so we could get the text in. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, if we could, first of all, go to the end of this document, we could see who the author of this document is. You see a name and a signature at the bottom of this document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Whose name appears at the bottom of this document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chief of the General Staff, Colonel-General Momcilo Perisic, which does not automatically mean that he is also the author.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Let me just ask you then, in terms --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we can go back to the first page of the English on this, if we could go to the top of the Serbian version on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is a document that is dated the 9th of November, 1995, and in the first paragraph we can see that the purpose of this document is to establish the responsibility and solve the status in service of professional soldiers of the VJ who served in the 40th Personnel Centre. And this document, Mr. Starcevic, you can see is an order. And if you turn to the Serbian language version, this is an order of the type which we discussed earlier, "naredjujem," so this is a command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if we turn to the second paragraph, the second item in this document, it deals with officers for whom it has been established that reasonable doubt exists that they had committed a violation of a discipline or a crime. Disciplinary investigation will be initiated through authorised officers, and it will be completed by the 20th of November, 1995. In respect of this text, Mr. Starcevic, is this consistent with the competencies and authorities of General Perisic as chief of the VJ General Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because he is the formal superior of them all and has the right of supervision of how his subordinate units execute their assignments. So this is a command to them to do something that they are supposed to do anyway. It's a kind of reminder or ultimately the command for this to be done right away within a certain dead-line.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And paragraph 3 deals with the regulation of these persons' status in the army, whether they should remain, or whether they should be terminated. Again, Mr. Starcevic, does that fall within the discretion of General Perisic as chief of the VJ General Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some cases, he does have the discretionary right pursuant to the already-mentioned Article 107 of the law, paragraph 2, to make a decision on the termination of service. But this paragraph doesn't talk about that, but actually requests that his assistants as part of their jurisdiction evaluate the results of disciplinary investigations and in accordance with their authority resolve the status in service pursuant to the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And, in fact, it say that they will make proposals to General Perisic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they would make proposals for some officers. As for others, they don't have to submit proposals, but can resolve the matter themselves because again, it seems to me, I did mention it a few times already, the order to the senior officers to resolve their status in service. And some officers do have the authority to regulate certain relations for specific soldiers of a certain rank and position or duty. In those cases, they could resolve that, but in cases when this exceeds their authority, they would submit the appropriate requests to the personnel administration. This is how I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this be given an Exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2413.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you. And that should be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 9474 on the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, you have not seen this document before coming into court, so, please, take your time to read it, and let me know if you get to the bottom, and when we get to the bottom, we need to turn the page on this document. Yours is only a one-page document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In respect of Your Honours, if you just let me know when we can turn to the next page. If we can go to the next page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, while the Judges are looking at the text, let me just identify this document for the record. This is a document from the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army office of the Chief of General Staff, it is dated the 11th of December, 1995. And can you tell us whose name appears it at the bottom of this document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document was signed by the Deputy Chief of the General Staff, Colonel-General Blagoje Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. This is a decision --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: First of all, let's go back to the first page in the English, if we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Starcevic, this is a decision to initiate a disciplinary investigation against Colonel Laza Babic, who was a commander in the 18th Corps during the period of 22 March, 1994, through 2 May, 1995, who was involved in criminal activities in the territory of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. We saw earlier from a previous document that the 18th Corps was a unit of the SVK. What I want to do with this particular document is ask you to comment, if you will, first of all, on Article 180, paragraph 1, of the Law on the Army, which appears to be one of the bases for this particular decision. Do you recall that, what that law is?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could take a look then at Article 180 very quickly, Prosecution Exhibit 197.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to look at it because I am not too fond of recalling legal documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. Starcevic, and we can give you some assistance on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could have that article in the English language as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is the basis for initiating a disciplinary investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And am I -- can you direct us to that particular portion of this article that gives the Colonel-General Kovacevic the authority to initiate such an investigation against an officer serving in the SVK -- who served in the SVK?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can tell you is that the ground for Kovacevic to initiate disciplinary proceedings, I would be able to tell you that, but this is the Army of the Serbian Republic of Krajina, or Article 180, or according to our law, Article 181, paragraph 1, item 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me is ask you, since this makes a reference to somebody who was serving in the 18th Corps, I think you've told us earlier, Mr. Starcevic, that there could be no disciplinary actions directed by the VJ against somebody in a separate army, would it be fair to assume, based on the content of this article, that Mr. Babic, Colonel Babic, was a VJ officer who was serving in the RSK at the time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is being led, and at the same time, is being asked for a conclusion that would constitute speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, I was trying to get directly to the point and put this document in the context of a previous answer that the witness had given and that we had debated earlier, that there was no authority to take disciplinary action against somebody from a different army. I'm asking him to draw a conclusion from the text of this -- in this document itself. While it may constitute some degree of speculation, I think that's quite a strong inference that can be drawn from the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From this question, Mr. Harmon is leaning towards it being a person from a different army. He is putting a question that does not arise from the document, and this witness can only talk about what is in the document because he is not testifying about this Babic on the basis of his personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll withdraw the question. I would ask that this document be admitted into evidence and given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am now objecting to the admission of this document because I think that Mr. Harmon did not meet the guide-lines of Article 27. He asked the witness to read something that is stated in the law and what is written in the document, but I think it is not a fact if the witness describes something that is stated in the document. I don't think that that constitutes a sufficient link between the witness and the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: May I, Your Honour, then just defer a decision on the admission of this document, and I'd like to go to another document, if I could. And I will make a link between the two documents, and then I will seek the admission of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me just go to my next exhibit. If I could have on the monitor, please, 65 ter 94 -- let me just see which one this is. 9476, please. I am sorry, 9474.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The one we've just had.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me get the right one. It is 94 -- bear with me for just a minute. It's 97 -- I am sorry. 9474 and it's page 5, so it's the same exhibit but page 5 of the English and page 4 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Again take a look at this document, Mr. Starcevic, if you could enlarge that for Mr. Starcevic, I'm sure he would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, the Registrar was chatting to me, is there anything that I ought to be doing?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, I just asked that the matter be placed on the monitor for us, and I asked Mr. Starcevic to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you have a chance to read it, Mr. Starcevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: First of all, let's identify whose name appears at the bottom right-hand side of the Serbian version of the document.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Deputy chief of the VJ General Staff for land forces, Lieutenant-General Nedeljko Copic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This document, sir, is document dated 22nd of December, 1995 and it relates to the disciplinary investigation of Colonel Babic, the individual whose name we saw on the previous document, on the previous decision, to initiate an investigation. And I want to direct your attention to the first paragraph, it says: "On the basis of the order by the Chief of General Staff of the Yugoslav Army ..." it gives a number, "... a disciplinary investigation has been initiated against Colonel Babic Laza..." again focusing on the word, the type of order in this case, it is a command, is it not? It uses the word "naredjenje," in the first line.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, again is the command issued by General Perisic to implement a disciplinary investigation against Colonel Babic something that he has the authority to do?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course he did have the authority, and judging by the first sentence, that is what he did, the command of the Chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army; but what it means is just the initiation of disciplinary investigations. It's not a command of the launching of proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, then I would ask that both these documents, this document and the previous document, be given an exhibit number and be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I abide by the same objection. We did not get anything from the witness in respect of these two documents except the witness reading from them. Mr. Harmon asked the witness to read something from the document, and the witness did that, and I think, thereby, Mr. Harmon did not meet the requirements of Article 27 of the guide-lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you have any answer, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour. The witness has examined both documents. The question that was put to the witness on the basis of both documents was whether or not General Perisic had the order to issue a command for a disciplinary investigation against Colonel Babic. And he has examined both of these documents, and on the basis of what he has seen in both of these documents, he has said yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Yes, answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What was asked is what was actually read from the document. I don't see anything more than what was read from the document. That is my objection. I think that no sufficient link is established between the witness. And the question whether General Perisic had the authority to issue this was the question which was put in relation to the first document which was admitted. These are document that we did not object to. As far as these two documents are concerned, Mr. Harmon did not put any other questions to the witness other than what actually was written in the document, and what the witness read out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm being advised by the Registrar that this document is part of 40 other documents. I'm not sure whether these are documents which have been previously tendered through another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, they have not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I believe they were -- just one minute, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, these are new documents. They have not been tendered through another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Then let me go to my next question. My next point is, I'm not sure whether Mr. Starcevic is here as a fact witness, trying to testify to documents that he has had dealings with before, or has he been talking about documents that he confirms comport with the legal position at the time when he was there, as he understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I can answer your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: A number of these documents, before Mr. Starcevic first gave his evidence in this court, he had an opportunity to review. These two documents, he has not had an opportunity to review. They were recently acquired. And they bear on issues that are directly relevant to these proceedings. That's why I have given Mr. Starcevic the opportunity to examine them, carefully examine them, and then try to -- and then get from him his opinion as to whether or not there's a legal basis for, one, the proceeding against Colonel Babic, the order issued by General Perisic. In this case, the decision, the first document, identifies Colonel Babic as somebody who was serving in the SVK. Also, it identifies crimes, potential crimes that is occurred on the territory of a different state. Now, the authority that the basis for starting that disciplinary investigation was a decision by General Perisic, and the question that I put to him under the light of these documents is: Did General Perisic have the authority and was it within his competence to order such an investigation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In trying to understand the objection, that's precisely what I'm trying to establish, because ever since Mr. Starcevic started testifying, even the previous time, I haven't heard any evidence of linking him specifically to a document by virtue of the requirements of guide-line 27. He has been telling us -- commenting on documents based on his knowledge of the law within the VJ. And I'm trying to understand where this objection emanates from now because we have admitted a number of documents through this witness after he had commented on them, even though he had not worked with them while he was in the army. He has only reviewed them when he came here, as you told us, and those that he hasn't had an opportunity to review before he came to court, you have given him an opportunity to review here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, I can't see how reviewing a document in court disqualifies him from establishing the link, if reviewing it out of court does establish it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm trying to clearly understand the nub of the objection, Mr. Lukic, because Mr. Starcevic has never tendered a document that he says, Yes, I have a link with this document. I wrote it, or I authored, I gave instructions that it be written, you know. And that is the link that is required in guide-line 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We all understand that Mr. Starcevic is a specific witness, and we know how you ordered him to be questioned and what answers he should give. The way I understand your guide-line is that there should be some connection between the witness and a document. I don't understand it as something that the witness has to be familiar with the facts. He just needs to understand it. Many of the documents discussed with the witness are already in evidence, so we had no objection to that. However, in these last two instances, we did not get anything more from Mr. Starcevic than what was written there. I don't think that the very fact that he only read what is written therein is sufficient to establish a connection. He is not a fact witness, and you said very precisely in your ruling that he can provide an opinion about things that he derives from experience. This is how I understood your decision when you determined these specific aspects of his testimonies. Now, in these two documents, I couldn't see anything beyond what he was reading. He was not -- and he is not a summary witness as he has been made into. And I think this is inconsistent with your ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you saying that his comments this afternoon are not in the nature of an opinion on the documents? You have just said: "He is not a fact witness, and you said very precisely in your ruling that he can provide an opinion about things that he derives from experience." Are you saying his answers on these two documents are not opinion?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These two documents go beyond his experience. The question posed by Mr. Harmon were simply reduced to his reading the document and getting himself familiar with what was written there. The questions posed by Mr. Harmon were just to confirm what was written there and to read what was written there. That was actually one step forward or beyond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's go back to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see a problem on page 62.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your objection started at page 59, line 12. Mr. Harmon said: "Q. Okay, now let me ask you this, since this makes a reference to somebody who was serving in the 18th Corps, I think you've told us earlier, Mr. Starcevic, that there could be no disciplinary actions directed by the VJ against somebody in a separate army?" Now, that's how he understood the law of the VJ at the time. "Would it be fair to assume based on the contents of this article that Mr. Babic, Colonel Babic was a VJ officer who was serving in the RSK at the time?" That's the question that was put, and that is, in my prima facie view, a perfectly legitimate question to ask this person who has come to testify based on his experience to give us guide-lines, guidance on what could or could not happen in the army. But I didn't want to intervene. I've looked at Mr. Harmon to answer you before I ruled on it, but based on the purpose for this witness specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you that this question could be put to this witness, but I don't think that the question and the answer have not established a connection between the witness and the document. And this is a legitimate question. We have no connection established between the document and the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then you and I are not even meeting. The connection that gets established is that -- lies therein, that he is able to opine on the document because he is here to give opinion based on his experience within the army. He doesn't have to have any other link with that -- he is coming here to interpret certain things to us according to the laws of the army. And those documents are documents which he may not necessarily have authored or which he may never have had any connection with before. He is something of a hybrid between 27 and something else. He is not here as a witness falling under 27, guide-line 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not what I read in the ruling. I'm viewing him as a fact witness, and I agree that all these questions could be put by construing guide-line 27 in terms of introduction and admission into evidence, that was my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then you are shifting from what you said a couple of minutes ago. What you said a couple minutes ago was precisely the opposite of that. You said, and I read it to you, you said: "He is not a fact witness and you said very precisely in your ruling that he can provide an opinion about things that he derives were experience," which is different from what you are saying now. Now you are saying he is a fact witness and must establish a link in guide-line 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is either erroneously translated or I misspoke. I know that according to your ruling, he is a fact witness, but he is entitled to speak about the things from his experience. That is how I interpret your decision. Based on his experience, he is entitled to proffer opinions. This is how I read your ruling. Now, since he has a specific status, and I really don't want to complicate this issue any further. I agree and accept that he can be asked these questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You've complicated it already. Mr. Lukic, any person, any witness who is given permission to give opinion evidence will necessarily not be bound to give an opinion on things that he has a prior connection with. Some of them he may, some of them he may not, necessarily. All that needs to happen is, you give him a set of facts, and you say these are the facts, and what is your opinion on the facts. Whether he knows though facts previously or not, provided those facts are within his area of expertise, whether the expertise derived from experience or academic qualification or otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully understand you, Your Honour. My position and my view is that regardless of his status in the courtroom, there has been no connection established between him and the document, not even on the basis of his opinion. Guide-line 27 didn't envisage --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think, in the interest of time, we are going to admitted it, mark it for identification; and I think you will later have to bring in that decision and argue. Let's see the basis on which the witness was called in for, because today you have given me two different bases for that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That was 9474, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: There are two separate documents, Your Honour. If I could just make the record clear, it's 9474 for both, it's 65 ter; but one document has an ET number that will help the Registrar. It is ET -- I'm not sure that will help the Registrar. Let me do this, let me defer with my colleague here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We can identify those through the assistance of Ms. Javier. I just want to admitted the two separate documents, the documents that I used in the course of the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is the one here by this Deputy Chief of General Staff, and the one prior.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Madam Registrar, are you able to remember which one, the one previous to this one is.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the first document of 65 ter 9474 was page 1 of the English and page 1 of the B/C/S version --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- which will be Exhibit P2414, marked for identification. And the second document, which is page 5 of the English version of 65 ter 9474 and page 4 of the B/C/S version of the same 65 ter number will be Exhibit P2415, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And there is no seal for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: These are both under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Both under seal. Both under seal, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. If I could have on the monitor please, 65 ter 9476, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, you have not seen this document either before coming into court. Just -- we will identify it, and we will take a look at the person who signs this document, and then, Mr. Starcevic, we will focus on the handwriting that is in the upper right-hand corner of the document in the Serbian language. But let's start just orienting ourselves in this document. First of all, if you would read the document, and if we could have the English. Yes, the first page at least, and then shortly in a few minutes turn to the second page in the English. If we could turn to the next page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, this is a document dated the 26th of September, 1995, and it emanates from the 11th Corps command. And you can identify the name of the person at the bottom left, who is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Corps commander, Major-General Dusan Loncar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you read the stamp at the lower right-hand side of the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we see its equivalent in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Received by the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, office of the Chief of the General Staff, number 17-267, 27th September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So this document is directed -- if we go back to the first page in the English. To whom is this document directed, Mr. Starcevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant-General Momcilo Perisic, personally. So personally to Lieutenant-General Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is a document, we can see in the second line, it's a report, reporting the unauthorized absence of certain officers from the 11th Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could go -- all of these officers were serving in the SVK, according to the content of this document; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to locate where it's written in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sir, if you take a look in each of the numbered paragraphs referring to specific individuals, it make references within each of those paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, this deals with a -- at the end, we can see the purpose of this document. It's a proposal to end the military service of those individuals, and it relies on Article 107, item 2 of the Law on the Army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if we could scroll down in the Serbian version of this document, I want to pay attention and like you to pay attention, Mr. Starcevic, to the handwriting in the upper right-hand corner of the document. If we can go to the English version, page 1, where there is a translation of that handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You see that portion that has some initials at the bottom of that text, that handwritten text?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see there are initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. What are those initials?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to me like MP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, assuming MP is Momcilo Perisic, the note directs something to be done. What is it that MP is directing in this circumstance?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that a this is addressed to Matovic [phoen] instructing him to investigate this and file criminal reports for the military court, provided they do not report to the unit by the 1st of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sir, does this request or this note to investigate and file criminal reports against the individuals that are listed in here, is that consistent with the competence and authority of General Perisic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is consistent to investigate the matter and file criminal reports, but I don't think that this is correct. This is a mistake because such reports are not to be sent to the disciplinary court, but rather to the criminal court.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And other than that one reservation, does this -- is this consistent with General Perisic's competencies as the Chief of General Staff to order an investigation and file criminal charges for the conduct that's described in this document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. He is expected to launch an initiative if the criminal charges are in question or to instruct disciplinary action to be taken before the disciplinary court.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that that document be admitted and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same objection as before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2416, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Starcevic, I'd like to turn to three documents in order. Actually, I need to check with the Registrar. If you could, first of all, I'd like to show 9549.01, but to show that doesn't identified the person who is referred to in the document, so I need to go to 9549 first, and then next -- sorry. Reminded it's 65 ter 9549, first of all. Is that page -- is that message that is on that screen "no page currently available" is -- there we go. I'm sorry. Can we go back to the first 9549 before we go to 01.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I apologise for the delay. The first page of this document is Prosecution Exhibit 2376. So this is only for purposes of introducing the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This is already an exhibit, this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is already an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 2376. Just the first page?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, do you have any medication?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll pass on these exhibits -- I am sorry, Your Honour, I'll pass on these for a moment. There appears to be some problem with the numbering of these exhibits. And I'll call up something else and we'll resolve this possibly tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 9439.02 on the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is a document, Mr. Starcevic. I am afraid it's a lengthy document. I know you have seen this before. And I'm going to have to direct you to certain pages in this document in order to possibly refresh your recollection. But this document is one of a set of documents that deal with the disciplining of a soldier, Captain Zoran Antic. I know you won't remember the details of this document, but let me orient you through this document, briefly. In the upper left-hand corner, Mr. Starcevic, this is a document from the military disciplinary court that is attached to the air force and anti-aircraft defence command. It is dated the 23rd of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And what I'd like to do is go to the last page of the document. If we could have the stamp on the right-hand side enlarged again for Mr. Starcevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Are you able, Mr. Starcevic, to read the text that encircles this stamp?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That is the air force and anti-aircraft defence command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is it the anti-air force and anti-aircraft command of the VJ or the VRS, or are you able to tell?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need to look at the top of the first page, but I think that this is the command -- just one moment. Could I please look at the first page. It's very difficult to decide because there is no reference to either one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can we go back to the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And maybe I can direct your attention to two features of this document that may assist you. Let me just show you, first of all, if we could enlarge again the stamp on this document. Now, this stamp appears to have a two-headed eagle in it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: To help because I took up sometime later, I think it's enough to show the witness the legal remedy, and then he will give a clear answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just see the legal remedy now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's where I'm going next, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Does that assist you, the legal remedy being the last text in the document, does that assist you, Mr. Starcevic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we see the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Judging by the fact that an appeal against this judgement may be lodged within -- to the -- submitted to the higher court, this is then the Army of Republika Srpska, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I take it that the legal remedy continues on the next page in the English version?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I take it that the English version does have the translation of the other stamp that I now see on the bottom left-hand corner of the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So these are -- this is a military disciplinary court in the VRS; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, this document, if we turn to page 2 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can we turn to page 2 of the English. And could we turn to the equivalent page in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: These people were found guilty of what, including Mr. Antic there, two accused, what were Mr. Antic and the other individual found guilty of in this case?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They left their unit without permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And their unit, according to this document, was in Banja Luka; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And for the sake of clarity, Banja Luka is in the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. We need to go to the next page in English, I believe, to see the sentence that is meted out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you see the sentence in B/C/S, in the Serbian language for Mr. Antic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What sentence did he receive in the VRS court proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They both were terminated from active duty service; Mr. Antic and Kanazir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Now, could this be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2417.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And that is not under seal, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could turn to a related document, which is 65 ter 9439.04.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sir, if you just review that document.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, can you identify whose name and what position is recorded at the bottom of this document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the post, but only the rank. This is for the 30th Personnel Centre, Colonel Gojko Mijic, signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. This document is a recommendation to end the professional military service of Mr. Antic, who we've seen in the previous document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the basis for the recommendation from Colonel Mijic is because Mr. Antic willfully abandoned his post for five consecutive days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please bring back the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It's paragraph 3 in the document.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This seems to be the ground for termination pursuant to this proposal, but what is stated in paragraph 3 is not -- does not correspond to the statement of reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's my problem too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I was now going to go to the statement of reasons, and I've some questions for you in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The first question I have is -- relates to the first sentence. It says: "The military disciplinary court attached to the command of the 30th Personnel Centre VJ issued," and it gives a reference number and a date, and that is the same reference number and date that was recorded on the previous document. My question -- my question to you is, can you assist us in understanding what a --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- VRS military disciplinary court -- how that conforms to the term attached to the 30th Personnel Centre of the VJ? Can you explain that to us?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to explain if I don't have the documents establishing those courts. I can just read what is written there, simply there is something confusing here because if we have seen the sentences before, that was the court of the air force and the PVO. But now in the statement of reasons, there is reference to a different court. I don't know if it's the same court, but Mr. Mijic made a mistake. I really am unable to tell from this document. It is also not clear to me what this -- these grounds are, the dual ones especially, not this Article 107, paragraph 1, item 2, because that would not be the grounds that would correspond to that kind of sentence or judgement. There's something confusing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me see if I can at least clarify something on this. Under the statement of reasons, one of the reasons they give is that there is a decision of a court, and it identifies specifically a judgement number I-Dis 37/95 of 23 September 1995. Now, the previous document was a VRS military disciplinary court decision that bears that same reference number and same date. So my first question is, can you explain to us on what basis a VJ soldier is being recommended for termination in the VJ on the basis of a VRS military disciplinary court decision?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot explain it in legal terms. This is something that is very difficult to base or to find legal grounds for, because if the -- he was a soldier of the Army of Yugoslavia, he could not have been tried by the disciplinary court, and if that disciplinary tried him, that cannot serve as the grounds for a termination of his service in the Army of Yugoslavia. So legally this is a little difficult to reconcile.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So to clarify, just the answer you gave me, Mr. Starcevic, you said: "If he was a soldier of the Army of Yugoslavia, he could not have been tried by the disciplinary court." Do you mean by the disciplinary court of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Right. And then finally, we'll conclude with this document because it's time for us to adjourn in a minute, the basis for his -- the recommendation to end his service state that he willfully abandoned his post and has not returned, and it gives as a basis, Article 107, paragraph 1, item 2, of the Law on the Army. Can you give us some assistance with what that article was? We've seen Article 107 --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would just like to know if that is the same article that we looked at, Article 107. I don't know the exact date though.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me just, if we can finally call that up very quickly just to confirm what this is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It is Prosecution Exhibit 197, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Article 107, and this is again confusing, because the proposal is drafted in such a way that there should -- that service should be terminated because he was absent from duty for five days. Those are the grounds it refers to. But in the statement of reasons, at the same time, it is stated that pursuant to the decision by the military disciplinary court, he was sentenced to termination from duties in the army. I think it is difficult to conclude what exactly is proper here, and the closest to my way of thinking is that Mr. Mijic did not recognise the judgement or the sentence by the military disciplinary court. And he decided to take Article 107, but instead of item 2, paragraph 2, he decided to refer to paragraph 4. But it's very difficult to tell what is what here. And it adds to the confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I see -- I am sorry, but you have referred to article -- sorry, you referred in your testimony just a minute ago to paragraph 4, and the text that I have in front of me says Article 107, paragraph 1, item 2, on the Law on the Army. So I'm a bit confused when you say paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm confused because Article 107, paragraph 1, item 2, is arbitrarily leaving service or the post. Paragraph 107, item 4 is the penalty of termination of service. In the statement of reasons, you have that a judgement was given or a sentence whereby his service is terminated, but pursuant to a proposal, this is not taken as the grounds for termination of service, but the grounds for that are item 2, as if there had been no proceedings before the military disciplinary court.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Starcevic, for clarifying that. Can this be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll give it an exhibit number and mark it for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2418, marked for identification, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Under seal, please, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That concludes for today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, you know the story, you don't discuss with anybody until you are excused from testifying. Are we still in private session? May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. We are going to take an adjournment very shortly, Mr. Starcevic, but again I must warn you, even though you do know, that you are not supposed to discuss it now that you are in the witness box until you are excused. We shall adjourn until tomorrow at quarter past 2.00, this time in Courtroom II. The Registrar says no, okay, we'll take the Registrar's word for it. It will be courtroom -- beg your pardon, it is 9.00, Mr. Starcevic, not 2.00. 9.00, Courtroom I. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 9th day of June, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.
